facts.raw_span: a 2-year history of progressive abdominal distension
accompanied by early satiety and urinary urgency
denied pain, weight loss, or systemic symptoms
her menstrual cycles were normal
her mother had a history of ovarian cysts
the abdomen was distended with dull percussion notes but without tenderness or guarding
a cyst measuring 16 × 24 cm
a large midline intraperitoneal cyst, 30 × 25.6 × 16.8 cm in size
the lesion had a fluid density of 20 Hounsfield units
demonstrated no calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations
laboratory studies, including α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, cancer antigen 19-9, and cancer antigen 125, were all within normal limits
the Risk of Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA) score was 4.1 %

concepts.why: The patient's mother had a history of ovarian cysts and the patient has a large midline intraperitoneal cyst, suggesting a possible ovarian cyst.
The cyst has a fluid density of 20 Hounsfield units and demonstrates no calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations, suggesting a benign simple cyst.
The patient has a large midline intraperitoneal cyst that compresses adjacent abdominal organs, suggesting a possible mesenteric cyst.
The patient has a large midline intraperitoneal cyst that extends from the liver to the pelvis, suggesting a possible peritoneal cyst.
The patient has a large ovarian cyst with a fluid density of 20 Hounsfield units, suggesting a possible mucinous cystadenoma.
The patient has a large ovarian cyst with a fluid density of 20 Hounsfield units, suggesting a possible serous cystadenoma.
The patient has a large midline intraperitoneal cyst that compresses adjacent abdominal organs, suggesting a possible giant abdominal cyst.
The low Risk of Malignancy Algorithm score explains the benign nature of the cyst.

rationales.F01: Progressive abdominal distension is a common symptom of ovarian cysts and other abdominal cysts.
rationales.F05: Family history of ovarian cysts increases the likelihood of ovarian cysts.
rationales.F07: A large cyst measuring 16 × 24 cm is highly suggestive of an ovarian cyst or other abdominal cyst.
rationales.F08: A large midline intraperitoneal cyst is highly suggestive of a peritoneal cyst or other abdominal cyst.
rationales.F10: The absence of calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations suggests a benign etiology.
rationales.F12: A low ROMA score suggests a low risk of malignancy, making benign ovarian cyst or other benign abdominal cyst more likely.
